summary: Iteration 3 backend + frontend regression after engine concurrency/cancel/LSH changes and new POST /api/scans/{scan_id}/cancel endpoint. Extended /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 2 new tests (test_cancel_scan_404, test_cancel_scan_on_live_scan). Ran full pytest against the live external URL: 10/10 PASS in ~9.7s. Covered: firm GET/PUT, clients CRUD + 404, seeded templates + template CRUD, file upload/list/soft-delete (incl. two byte-identical CSVs, profit_and_loss_2022.csv, receipt.png), full scan pipeline queued->scanning->completed with progress=100 and counts.exact_duplicate>=1, wrong_period>=1, missing_doc>=1, unreadable>=1, findings PATCH persists status='keep', CSV/XLSX/PDF reports non-empty with correct content-types, and NEW cancel endpoint: 404 on unknown scan_id, {ok:true} on live scan with terminal state 'completed' (small scan finished before cancel took effect — acceptable per spec, endpoint responded correctly and did not break the scan). Frontend smoke: LedgerLens loads on external URL, all nav data-testids present (nav-dashboard/clients/scan_workspace/checklists/review_center/file_compare/reports), Firm Setup shows persisted TEST_Firm from backend tests, no console errors. No regressions detected.

issues: Emergent ve-dynamic wrapper injects <span> inside <option> causing hydration warnings — pre-existing, not from this iteration.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py cancel_scan: returns 'cancelling' status message even when scan is already completed/error (not in queued/scanning). Harmless but the JSON status field is misleading; consider returning the actual current status.

CANCEL_REQUESTS is a module-level set with no bounds — fine for single-user local app but should be pruned on scan completion/error (currently only discarded in _run_scan finally). Verified discard is called in success/error paths.
Pre-existing (not this iter): _run_scan uses asyncio.get_event_loop() (deprecated preferred: get_running_loop()); list_clients N+1; delete_client not atomic. Main agent may schedule cleanup.
